reasoning: The two attempts are nearly identical and both correct. A frees the occupied cell in a Destroying handler, so the cell is released however the block is removed, and it adds an IsA BasePart check and a client-side filter by owner. B only cleans up on the RemoveBlock path and has a misleading comment about how its table is keyed.

criteria.note: Removal is added to BlockPlacement.server.luau and BlockPlacer.luau in their existing style, with shared checkRate/isInReach helpers and no new framework.
The server keeps a blockInfo[part] table with ownerUserId and rejects anyone else; the OwnerUserId attribute only lets the client filter which blocks it asks about.
Checks typeof Instance, IsA BasePart and table membership (which stands in for the Blocks-folder check), plus checkRate and isInReach on info.cell; a Destroying:Once handler clears occupied[cell].
MouseButton2 counts as a click only when the drag distance is 6 px or less and the hold is under 0.4 s; TouchLongPress on Begin with one touch removes; UI-processed input is ignored.
Placement logic is unchanged apart from the shared helpers, and all checks pass.
Changes stay in the two placement files, with isRateLimited/isInReach helpers and a waitForRemote helper.
placedBlocks[part].PlacerUserId is compared against player.UserId on the server.
Checks typeof plus table membership, rate and reach, and clears occupied in onRemoveBlock, but blocks destroyed any other way leak their entry and keep the cell occupied.
Right-click counts only when the drag is 4 px or less; TouchLongPress on Begin removes; gameProcessed input is respected.
Placement still works and all checks pass; one comment wrongly says the table is keyed by UserId.

strengths: Freeing the cell on Destroying works however the block goes away
Client only targets its own blocks via the attribute, while the server trusts only its own table
Holding right-click longer than 0.4 s doesn't remove, which further separates clicks from camera drags
weaknesses: The attribute name is duplicated between client and server instead of living in a shared module

strengths: Clean, minimal implementation with sound server checks
One shared rate limit covers placing and removing
weaknesses: Cell and table cleanup happens only on the RemoveBlock path
Misleading comment about what the table is keyed by
Client fires the remote for any block, including other players' blocks (the server rejects them)
